div.div: 7 انسحج It had its outer integument, or superficial part, abraded, or otherwise removed: (S, K:) said of the skin: (S:) [and it seems from the phrase سَحَجُ الفَخِذَيْنِ occurring in the O and K in art. بذح, that ↓ سَحِجَ , inf. n. سَحَجٌ, may signify the same: but سَحَجُ may there be a mistranscription for سَحْجُ.] One says, اِنْسَحَجَ جِلْدُهُ مِنْ شَىْءٍ مَرَّ بِهِ His skin had its cuticle abraded in consequence of a thing that passed by him. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
